Concept premise Storyboard sketches are AI-generated

First Take, No Notes, No Edits

Emma Myers, whose whole career is built on nailing a performance in the moment, turns the camera on herself between scenes and shoots her actual day on a Galaxy S27 Ultra. One take. Natural light. Whatever the lens catches is what goes up.

1
Opening
First 0-3s
Emma in a plain green-room chair, script pages on her lap, window light falling across her face
  • Cut straight to Emma mid-thought, no intro card, no music swell, just her voice saying ‘I never reshoot this stuff’
  • Snap-zoom onto the Galaxy S27 Ultra resting on the script, camera UI visible on screen
2
Development
Mid
Emma steps outside into an ordinary daylit street or studio back-lot, Galaxy in hand, filming whatever she notices
  • Pan across the scene as Emma zooms in on a distant detail, the phone’s optical zoom ring visible on screen for a beat
  • Cut to the unedited still on her camera roll, no filter badge, no edit history, just the raw capture filling the frame
3
Closing
End
Emma looks directly into the phone camera, the captured photo still glowing on screen behind her reflection in a window
  • Slow-mo reveal of Emma’s expression the moment she sees the shot, unhurried, no voiceover
  • Cut to a static card: the photo full-bleed, the hashtags fading in as plain white text, no additional treatment
Do / Don't · Powered by Insight Lens

Content Creation Guide

Do/don't production guidance across 4 areas, grounded in the selected influencer's high-performing content.
Concept & Hook
  • Shoot on a real Wednesday or A Good Girl’s Guide set, not a Samsung pop-up or event floor
  • Time it to a moment in Emma’s world — an episode drop or a Forbes honoree week
  • Anchor it in Emma’s behind-the-scenes voice, not an Unpacked reveal or stage moment
Production & Editing
  • Open on Emma’s face and voice together, narrating a candid moment from set
  • Put the S27 Ultra in her hand in the thumbnail, against an editorial backdrop
  • Run it long enough to breathe — her unhurried storytelling needs the room
Product & Message
  • Show optical zoom pulling detail from real daylight, no filters after the fact
  • Show the camera UI once — shutter or zoom ring — as proof it’s a first take
  • No Generative Edit or AI retouch — her last Galaxy post leaned on it, this campaign is the opposite
Caption & Distribution
  • Write a longer caption in her own voice, pulled from the reel’s story
  • Stack the mandatory tags with longer, descriptive ones from her film world
  • Carry all four required hashtags — don’t trim for a cleaner look
Concept & Hook
  • Hook in the first second with the snap from classic to trendy
  • Play it as a style duel and ask viewers to pick a side
  • Don't open on a logo or an unboxing — she loses the scroll
Production & Editing
  • Film full-screen 9:16 and match-cut on every outfit switch
  • Keep it under 30 seconds so the loop replays the reveal
  • Avoid static talking-head stretches between locations
Product & Message
  • Stand the Fold in Flex Mode so Emma films herself hands-free
  • Show Galaxy AI restyling the shot live, not in a caption
  • Don't read out specs — let the split screen do the talking
Caption & Distribution
  • Use a trending sound and put the question on screen
  • Post in the evening and pin a comment asking for their pick
  • Don't bury the question under hashtags — three campaign tags only

Creative ConceptOne video idea, beat by beat, with do’s and don’ts for each platform
Concept premise

One Street, Two Eras

Jordan walks one neighborhood from breakfast to midnight and films every stop twice: once the way a guidebook would frame it, once the way his followers would post it. The Galaxy Z Fold8 is where the two takes meet.

1
Opening
First 0-3s
Jordan at a corner café at sunrise, the Fold8 unfolded on two versions of the same storefront.
  • Hold on the split screen for a beat
  • Snap to Jordan: 'Which one would you visit?'
2
Development
Mid
Three stops across the day; at each, a tripod classic shot and a handheld trendy shot.
  • Chapter card with each stop's name
  • Galaxy AI restyles one frame per stop on screen
3
Closing
End
A rooftop at night, all six frames tiled across the unfolded screen.
  • Jordan picks his favorite pair
  • End card: the full route, pinned in the comments
Do / Don't · Powered by Insight Lens

Content Creation Guide

Do/don't production guidance across 4 areas, grounded in the selected influencer's high-performing content.
Concept & Hook
  • Open on the finished classic-vs-trendy split of the best stop, then rewind
  • Build the episode as one neighborhood, morning to night
  • Don't open on the unboxing; his viewers came for the city
Production & Editing
  • Film the classic take on a tripod, the trendy take handheld
  • Keep each chapter under 90 seconds so viewers can jump to a stop
  • Keep music out from under his narration; the voiceover carries retention
Product & Message
  • Unfold the Z Fold8 at every stop to compare both takes side by side
  • Show Galaxy AI restyling one frame per stop, not every frame
  • Don't read the spec list on camera
Caption & Distribution
  • Put the neighborhood first in the title and the device second
  • Pin a comment listing every stop in order
  • Don't add more tags than the three campaign hashtags
Concept & Hook
  • Lead with the trendy frame and reveal the classic on the next swipe
  • Don't split the two takes into separate posts
Production & Editing
  • Shoot each pair from the same spot and height
  • Keep text off the classic frame
Product & Message
  • Show the Fold's split screen on slide three
  • Don't tag product features on every slide
Caption & Distribution
  • Ask followers which take they'd visit first
  • Don't post before noon; his saves peak in the evening

Creative ConceptOne video idea, beat by beat, with do’s and don’ts for each platform
Concept premise

Thrift Once, Style Twice

Nina finds one vintage piece and styles it twice in the same mirror: once the way it was worn when it was made, once the way her feed wears it now. The Z Fold8's cover screen is her mirror.

1
Opening
First 0-3s
Nina in the mirror, the outfit split down the middle by a hard cut.
  • Freeze on the split for half a second
  • On-screen text: 'same jacket, 1995 vs. 2026'
2
Development
Mid
Beat-synced switches between the two looks, the Fold8 flipping open for each photo.
  • Galaxy AI grades the trendy photo on screen
  • Both photos side by side on the unfolded screen
3
Closing
End
Both photos on the unfolded screen, held up to the mirror.
  • Caption vote: classic or trendy?
  • Loop back to the opening split
Do / Don't · Powered by Insight Lens

Content Creation Guide

Do/don't production guidance across 4 areas, grounded in the selected influencer's high-performing content.
Concept & Hook
  • Start mid-transition: half classic outfit, half trendy
  • Keep the 'one piece, two eras' format she's known for
  • Don't open with a talking-head intro
Production & Editing
  • Cut on the beat for every outfit switch
  • Film in one mirror spot so each switch reads instantly
  • Keep it under 25 seconds
Product & Message
  • Use the Fold8's cover screen as her mirror-selfie viewfinder
  • Let Galaxy AI suggest the trendy color grade on screen
  • Don't hold the phone up to the lens as a product shot
Caption & Distribution
  • Post at lunchtime, when her views per reach run highest
  • Caption it as a vote: classic or trendy?
  • Skip trending sounds that drown out the switch cue
Concept & Hook
  • Post the two looks as a before/after carousel
  • Don't crop the outfit at the knees
Production & Editing
  • Match the lighting across both photos
  • Avoid heavy beauty filters
Product & Message
  • Show the cover screen in the mirror shot
  • Don't add a separate product-only slide
Caption & Distribution
  • Tag the thrift store; her followers ask where every piece is from
  • Don't post on weekday mornings

Creative Concept One video idea, beat by beat, with do’s and don’ts for each platform
Concept premise

The Grade Was the Light

Kyle Nutt builds his vintage look in post: the LUT, the grade, the halation. This film takes the software away and sends him out at the one hour when the light already does it, shooting a single unbroken take on a Galaxy S27 Ultra. No grade, no cut. The colour is whatever the sun was doing.

1
Opening
First 0-3s
Kyle at his desk in the dark, a finished grade still open on the monitor behind him
  • Open on the graded frame on his monitor, then he closes the laptop mid-sentence
  • Snap to the Galaxy S27 Ultra already recording in his hand, camera UI live, nothing set up
2
Development
Mid
A street an hour before sunset, the light doing what his LUT usually does
  • One unbroken walk as he zooms to a far window catching the last of the sun
  • He names the setting out loud, no filter and no grade, while the frame stays warm on its own
3
Closing
End
The same street behind him, the untouched still already on the phone screen
  • Hold the raw still up against the real street and let the two match
  • End on an export with no adjustment layers, the panel empty, then cut to black
Do / Don't · Powered by Insight Lens

Content Creation Guide

Do/don't production guidance across 4 areas, grounded in the selected influencer's high-performing content.
Concept & Hook
  • Frame it as a one-take challenge to himself, the filmmaker who cannot cut
  • No test footage or B-roll cutaways, the reel is the take start to finish
  • Open on the shot he would normally reject, and keep it
Production & Editing
  • Hand-held, no gimbal, let the camera’s own stabilisation carry the walk
  • No colour grade, no LUT, no transitions, the export is the capture
  • Let one focus hunt or exposure shift stay in, it is the proof
Product & Message
  • Show the zoom ring pulling a far detail he would normally reach with a lens
  • Hold on the camera UI for a beat so the capture reads as live
  • No Generative Edit or AI retouch, even to fix a frame he dislikes
Caption & Distribution
  • Caption it as a tutorial note: what the camera did, not what an edit would
  • Stack the four required tags with his usual filmmaking and gear tags
  • Don’t trim the hashtag set down for a cleaner grid
Concept & Hook
  • Open mid-walk with the camera already rolling, no title card
  • No watch-till-the-end bait, the payoff is that nothing was fixed
  • Say out loud in the first second that this is the only take
Production & Editing
  • Vertical full-screen, under 30 seconds, one continuous run
  • No speed ramps, no jump cuts, no editing-app templates
  • Keep the native audio, wind and steps and shutter, over a trending sound
Product & Message
  • Zoom to a subject across the street and hold, so the reach is obvious
  • Flash the camera UI on screen once as the shutter fires
  • Don’t recite specs, show what the lens reached instead
Caption & Distribution
  • Put the one-take claim on screen as plain text, not a sticker
  • Carry all four campaign tags alongside his filmmaking tags
  • Don’t move the tags into a pinned comment
Concept & Hook
  • Build it as a short tutorial: one location, one take, what the camera handled
  • No multi-location edit, the constraint is the format
  • State the rule in the first ten seconds so the run makes sense
Production & Editing
  • Publish the unbroken take as the body of the video
  • No colour pass, no stabilisation in post, no music bed over the take
  • Pull the thumbnail straight from the take, ungraded
Product & Message
  • Narrate the zoom as he uses it, the way he narrates a lens choice
  • Keep the camera UI in frame long enough to read at 1080p
  • No competing camera or rig in shot, even as a comparison
Caption & Distribution
  • Put the four required tags in the first two lines of the description
  • Write the description as tutorial notes, with the settings he used
  • Don’t upload an edited highlights cut during the same window
Concept & Hook
  • Lead with the plain claim: one take, no edit, shot on a phone
  • No cross-posted caption that still says link in bio
  • Frame it for an audience meeting his work for the first time
Production & Editing
  • Upload natively at full length rather than a trimmed teaser
  • No burned-in auto captions over the take
  • Make the opening frame read with the sound off
Product & Message
  • Name the Galaxy S27 Ultra once, in the first sentence
  • Keep the zoom pull and the camera UI in one continuous shot
  • No Generative Edit or AI retouch, the same as every other platform
Caption & Distribution
  • Write two or three plain sentences, no filmmaker shorthand
  • Include all four required hashtags even though the platform buries them
  • Don’t post it as a link out to the YouTube cut

Creative Concept One video idea, beat by beat, with do’s and don’ts for each platform
Concept premise

As They Came

Zina waits for the frame where Lilly and Lucy look their best, then posts that one. This film keeps whatever the first take caught: the yawn, the turned back, the cat that walks off mid-shot. Filmed at home on a Galaxy S27 Ultra in the window light they already sleep in. The rescues came as they were, and so does the footage.

1
Opening
First 0-3s
Zina on the floor by the window, phone already rolling, Lilly asleep and Lucy ignoring her
  • Open with the camera already running, no setup and nobody called over
  • Lucy walks out of frame in the first seconds and the shot stays exactly where it is
2
Development
Mid
Late morning light across the rug, Zina still while the cats move through the frame
  • Zoom across the room to Lilly’s paw without standing up and waking her
  • One beat on the camera UI as the shutter fires, the room lit by the window alone
3
Closing
End
The unedited photo on screen, Lucy finally back in her lap
  • Hold on the raw frame, soft and slightly off, with neither cat looking at the lens
  • End on her hand in Lucy’s fur, no voiceover and no music
